output.subject: Thank you for your kind words about our Elm & 4th branch
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

We are so sorry for the loss of your father. Thank you for taking the time to write to us during what must be a very difficult period.

You told us you had been dreading closing out your dad's accounts, and that our colleague at the Elm & 4th branch walked you through every step. You mentioned they found a CD that none of your family knew about, and that they called you back when one of your forms was kicked back. It means a great deal to hear that someone helped make this process feel more manageable for you.

We have received your message, and a specialist team is reviewing it. We will respond within 10 business days. If any questions come up as you finish settling your father's affairs, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

With our sincere condolences and thanks,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a compliment, not a complaint; the reply thanks the customer, confirms receipt, says a specialist team is reviewing it and gives the 10-business-day timeframe. Confirm this fits a thank-you message.
The staff member's name is redacted and the reply refers to 'our colleague'; decide whether to name them.
Decide whether to tell the customer that their thanks will be passed to the staff member and branch.
The customer is recently bereaved; check whether any estate or account-closure steps, including the CD that was found, are still pending.
